_note: The MAINNET deployment of the channel contract, as a record a reader can re-derive.
Same purpose as `sepolia.json`: a public document can cite a file instead of restating a hex
string, and the deployment's own working files are gitignored, so without this record the tree
cannot show that the contract exists and 'absent from tracked source' reads as 'not deployed'.
Every value below was read from a node with the query beside it, not copied from a document.
Re-derive it: run the queries in `verified_by` against `rpc` and compare.
THE CLASS HASH IS NOT SEPOLIA'S. Sepolia carries 0x07d2f324…4467, the version with a `u64`
counter in storage; that counter was removed before this deployment, so mainnet carries a
different class. `scarb build && sncast utils class-hash --contract-name Channel` on the
tracked source reproduces the value below, which is the check that this record is honest.
This is NOT strk20.json. That file wants three mainnet hashes each proving a real call against
the STRK20 pool. This deploys our own contract and moves no value through any pool, so it
belongs here and would be a false claim there.

deployed_by._type_note: INVOKE because the deploy went through an account, via the universal deployer. It is the transaction that deployed the contract; calling it 'the deploy transaction' is loose.

_note: Paid, not estimated. Predicted from a local devnet rehearsal before spending: declare 0.5842,
deploy 0.0347. Both came in 1.6% and 7% under. `l1_gas` was 0 on every transaction, so none
of this is exposed to Ethereum L1 gas.
The account itself was counterfactual — funded but never deployed — so its DEPLOY_ACCOUNT is
part of what this deployment cost and is recorded rather than netted out.

verified_by: starknet_call(<contract.address>, selector('privacy_invoke'), [0x1234, 0x5678]) -> ['0x0'] — the empty open-note deposits array a pool-routed publish requires
